  570. Mesquite smoke gives Texas barbecue its distinctive flavor.
  571. Hickory-smoked bacon is a classic of Southern cooking.
  572. Cedar planks are used to grill salmon with a gentle fragrance.
  573. Bay laurel leaves flavor soups and stews around the world.
  574. Allspice berries come from a tropical evergreen tree.
  575. Cloves are the dried flower buds of a tropical tree.
  576. Nutmeg and mace both come from the same tree's fruit.
  577. The spice trade shaped history as nations sought these precious tree products.
  578. Vanilla grows on a vine but often climbs on trees in the tropics.
  579. Tamarind pods contain a tangy pulp used in cooking across Asia and Africa.
  580. Moringa leaves are rich in nutrients and eaten in many tropical countries.
  581. Baobab fruit powder is high in vitamin C.
  582. Shea trees yield butter used in cooking and skin care across West Africa.
  583. Karité groves are traditionally managed by village women.
  584. Marula fruit is a favorite of elephants and also made into a liqueur.
  585. Wild harvesting of tree products provides income for forest communities.
  586. Community forestry gives local people a stake in protecting woodlands.
  587. Studies show that forests managed by Indigenous communities often lose less cover.
  588. Land rights and forest health are closely connected.
  589. Planting trees is most effective when the right species go in the right places.
  590. Trees planted in grasslands or peatlands can sometimes do more harm than good.
  591. Protecting existing forests is generally cheaper and faster than regrowing them.
  592. A single large tree can be worth thousands of dollars in services to a city.
  593. These services include cooling, stormwater control, and cleaner air.
  594. Cities now keep inventories of their street trees and plan for their care.
  595. Diverse planting protects a city against the loss of any one species.
  596. Giving trees enough soil volume is the key to a long life in a paved street.
  597. Soil cells and structural soil let roots grow beneath sidewalks.
  598. Trees bring beauty, habitat, shade, and meaning to nearly every place people live.
  599. A walk beneath old trees reminds us how much time a living thing can hold.
  600. Whoever plants a tree gives a gift that may outlast them by centuries.
